questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Plotly charts over matplotlib charts for business presentations?
options: Plotly renders charts faster on large datasets
Plotly charts are interactive—users can hover, zoom, and filter in the browser
Plotly produces higher-resolution static images
Plotly requires less code to produce the same charts
questions.explanation: Plotly generates HTML-based interactive charts. Stakeholders can hover to see exact values, zoom into date ranges, and toggle series on/off—all without any code. This interactivity makes exploratory discussions far more productive than static images.

questions.question: Which Plotly Express function creates an interactive bubble chart where bubble size represents a third variable?
options: px.scatter(df, x='gdp', y='life_exp', size='population')
px.bubble(df, x='gdp', y='life_exp', z='population')
px.circle(df, x='gdp', y='life_exp', radius='population')
px.plot(df, type='bubble', x='gdp', y='life_exp')
questions.explanation: `px.scatter()` with the `size` parameter creates a bubble chart. The `size` argument maps a numeric column to bubble area, encoding a third dimension. This pattern is used by analysts to show relationships between GDP, life expectancy, and population simultaneously.

questions.question: What does `fig.update_layout(title='Revenue Dashboard', xaxis_title='Month')` do in Plotly?
options: Creates a new figure with the specified title and axis labels
Updates an existing figure's title and x-axis label in place
Saves the figure to an HTML file named 'Revenue Dashboard'
Adds a second plot with the x-axis labeled 'Month'
questions.explanation: `fig.update_layout()` modifies properties of an existing Plotly figure object without recreating it. It follows a method-chaining pattern common in Plotly—you build the chart with `px.*`, then refine it with `update_layout()`, `update_traces()`, etc.

questions.question: A Plotly choropleth map colors countries based on a numeric value. What data does it require?
options: Latitude and longitude coordinates for every data point
ISO country codes (or names) and a numeric value to encode as color
A GeoJSON file with custom drawn boundaries
A pre-built map image as the chart background
questions.explanation: Plotly's built-in choropleth maps require only standard ISO country codes (e.g., 'USA', 'GBR') and a numeric column for the color scale. Plotly handles the geography internally. This makes it easy to create global sales maps from any country-level dataset.

questions.question: When would you use `fig.write_html('dashboard.html')` instead of `fig.show()`?
options: When the chart is too large to display in a notebook
When you want to share an interactive chart with someone who doesn't have Python installed
When you need a higher-resolution image for printing
When you want to embed the chart in a pandas DataFrame
questions.explanation: `fig.write_html()` exports the chart as a self-contained HTML file with all interactivity intact. Anyone can open it in a browser—no Python, Plotly, or internet connection required. This is the standard way to share Plotly dashboards with non-technical stakeholders.
